thread:
leo: Quick design review for scorecard approval modal + focus trap issues. Mock here: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE-scorecard. Main asks: ensure keyboard users don't get stuck, and copy for bulk-approve needs clarification.

nina: Saw a trap when tabbing backward from the confirm button 100 -> focus lands behind modal. Repro: open scorecard, select 3 items, press Shift+Tab repeatedly.

kari: Hmm that suggests the invisible overlay element might be tabbable. We should ensure overlay has tabindex='-1' and inert when modal is open.

dez: Also microcopy: current header says "Approve changes" which feels ambiguous. Suggest "Approve selected scorecards" or "Approve selected diffs" depending on context. Which one matches product language elsewhere?

mike: Product copy elsewhere uses "selected changes" in rollout flow. I vote for consistency: "Approve selected changes" but add a small subline: "This applies only to the items selected above."

a11ybot: Automated audit: Modal label missing aria-labelledby; focus order: confirmed trap due to .overlay receiving focus. Recommendations: role='dialog' with aria-modal='true', focus trap managed with JavaScript, and add aria-describedby for subline. Contrast check: confirm button text meets 4.5:1 on default state.

leo: Good catches. Kari can you propose DOM attributes? Also we should consider Escape closing: should Escape both close and clear selection? I think close only. Clearing selection surprises people.

kari: Agreed. Proposed attributes: <div role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="modal-title" aria-describedby="modal-desc"> overlay: aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1" inert (polyfill). Focus management: on open save activeElement, focus first tabbable in modal, on close restore.

nina: For keyboard flows, add a visible focus ring on the secondary 'Cancel' button for clarity. Designers: avoid using outline: none.

dez: Copy proposal for the subline: "Approves only the items you selected. To update the prompt set, use Rollout." Short, actionable.

mike: Small UX nit: when approving multiple scorecards, we should show a compact summary: "Approving 3 items: 2 pass, 1 regression" so users know counts. If there are regressions require a confirmation checkbox "I understand this will apply changes that include regressions." Might be heavy-handed though.

leo: I like the summary. For regressions maybe a highlighted warning row with link to view diffs. Avoid forced confirmation unless high-risk flag set. Add a telemetry event if user approves with regressions.

a11ybot: When showing dynamic summary counts, ensure live region updates with aria-live='polite' so screen readers get updates when selection changes.

kari: Also ensure modals stacked: if user opens help from modal we shouldn't trap twice. Use modal stack manager.

nina: One more microcopy ask: change disabled approve tooltip from "Select items to continue" to "Select at least one item to approve." Slightly clearer.

dez: I'll prototype the modal DOM and focus management, push PR with unit tests for focus restore. Estimate: 1 day.

mike: I'll draft copy patch and add the summary text variations for 1/2/3+ items.

leo: Action list: kari implement aria attrs + focus trap; dez implement modal stack + tests; mike update copy; nina verify keyboard tab order + focus styles; a11ybot will re-run audit after PR. Review sync tomorrow 10am PT. Thanks! :white_check_mark:
